prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and active form of glucagon-like peptide-1 that made incretin-based therapy of diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: a single-part B041 prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 showed that the six of us converge on the same names, but the reason I hold it is scientific. Holst established the incretin effect and GLP-1 secretion in humans, Drucker defined proglucagon processing and the biology of the derived peptides, and Mojsov identified the truncated bioactive form. That chain explains why the later agonists work, and the mechanism has been confirmed independently in large outcome trials covering glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal endpoints. The prize is for what was discovered about the hormone, and the citation can say plainly that this made incretin-based therapy possible without naming the drug programme. The case is mature, and I see no argument from timing for waiting.
statement.case_against: The attribution weakness is still the main one and the round-1 exchange did not remove it. Habener is outside the credited names, Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested, and the three-person cap leaves out Knudsen, whose acylated analogues are what reached patients. None of us can adjudicate the priority record from the permitted files, so my support for Mojsov rests on the credited evidence as supplied and not on a settled history. I would revisit the third name only on documented evidence that her claim fails, not on recollection. Long-term safety of chronic therapy is still accumulating, but it concerns the drugs and not the discovery.

responses.point: Sandberg now accepts the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio but still regards Knudsen's long-acting acylated analogue programme as a distinct achievement and not a later engineering detail, and he argues that the citation can carry the drug history.
responses.response: I accept that Knudsen's step was distinct and that obesity therapy would not exist without it, so I do not call it a detail. My disagreement is with using the citation to cover it. A citation that credits the drug programme while naming no one from it would read as hollow, and one that names her would require a fourth person or a displaced discoverer. I would keep the wording to the physiology and the active peptide, say that this made incretin-based therapy possible, and accept that the drug step is honoured only indirectly. That is a real cost and I would rather state it than hide it.

responses.point: Linnarsson holds that if the committee wants the translational component, Knudsen should replace Mojsov and not become a fourth name, and he ranks CAR-T second because durable remissions are the kind of human benefit this prize rewards.
responses.response: I agree with the substitution logic, and it is the right way to frame the choice: a swap of Mojsov for Knudsen, never a fourth name. I would only make that swap if the committee decided that the prize should reward the drug and not the hormone, and I do not think the record supports that. On CAR-T I agree it is a new modality with real benefit and that Eshhar's absence bears on who we name, not on its rank. That is exactly why I still put it behind B041. I cannot form a three-name set that I am comfortable defending, since the June, Sadelain and Rosenberg lineages are different contributions.

responses.point: The chair's summary asks whether the committee will adjudicate the Mojsov and Habener priority record, whether the citation should cover the hormone or also the analogue programme, and whether any second part can share the prize.
responses.response: On the first question, I do not think we can adjudicate priority from this record and I would not claim to. The fair course is to keep the three names as credited and let the citation say what was discovered without asserting who was first. On the second, I would restrict it to the hormone physiology and active peptide. On the third, no second part works for me: any second achievement forces one of the three discoverers out, and I would not weaken B041 for a modest gain. If B041 stands alone, my next candidate is B011, then B023, for the reasons below.

responses.point: Perlmann regards the unfolded protein response as a stable 25-year-old mechanism with the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, and he notes the tension between a second part and the three-person cap.
responses.response: I still agree on the attribution and the stability of the mechanism, and I maintain B011 as my first alternative. What I would need before ranking it higher is a clearer human consequence, since the disease links are still largely indirect. Linnarsson makes the same point. I do not treat that as a reason to leave it out, because a basic cell-biology prize can be as defensible as any physiology prize, but it is easier to defer than B041. Your point about the cap is right: adding Walter and Mori would cut Mojsov or Holst, and I would not do that.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius keeps B044 and B023 as the next strongest cases, as therapeutic modalities whose principle is confirmed clinically, and she says the committee may reasonably decide that the priority dispute makes the B041 credit too contentious to resolve fairly.
responses.response: I take her last point seriously, since a contested credit can damage a strong case. But I do not think contention should make us withhold recognition from a discovery this large, because three well-supported names remain even if one claim is disputed. Of the two clinical alternatives, I still find B044 clean but narrower in principle than B023. B023 has the larger conceptual step but the less settled attribution, so neither moves ahead of B011 for me. If she can name evidence from the record that weakens Mojsov specifically, I would change the third name.

uncertainties: Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide and Habener's contribution cannot be verified from the permitted files, so the third name rests on the supplied credit and not on a documented history.
Whether the committee should treat the drug-development step as a distinct prize-worthy achievement. I have excluded it, and that choice leaves Knudsen outside the prize.
Which alternative is next if B041 stands alone. I rank B011 first, but B023 would rise if a defensible laureate set without Eshhar could be found.
How much weight long-term safety data for chronic incretin therapy should carry. I judge it not to affect the core discovery.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate is apparent from my profile. I co-authored a 2009 paper with Thomas Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons and a 2019 review with Sten Grillner. Neither relates to a shortlisted ballot, so I see no reason for recusal. Nothing in the round-1 exchange changes this.
